thread:
maya: Drafting a compact GA checklist for Dedicated reserved pools. Need quick feedback on launch gating criteria and what to include in the SE kickoff.

drew: Core ask: explicit SLOs per commit tier (latency P95/P99) and a clear statement of burst grace window + how long we SDR (soft degrade routing) lasts. Customers always want numbers.

vijay: Add KV cache warm/cold expectations and a line about quantized fallback quality delta. Also include the billing visibility header (how we report burst token consumption).

maya: Agreed. Draft checklist below — keep it under 6 bullets to be SE-friendly:

1) Confirm reservation: pool size, region, model family, and peak QPS estimate.
2) SLA summary: P95 and P99 latency targets for committed pool; min token throughput floor.
3) Burst policy: soft-burst window (e.g., 3m) then best-effort for next X mins; sustained >5m triggers fallback routing to compatible model variant (expect ~30-80ms tail increase depending on model).
4) Prewarm & cache: scheduled prewarm vs predictive; KV-cache cold-start penalty (approx +100ms first warmup per shard).
5) Fallback & rollback: who activates fallback (oncall), notification script for SEs, and post-incident follow-up window (24-72h).
6) Billing & telemetry: how burst tokens show up on billing, and where to find per-route latency and token breakdowns.

drew: For the SE script, propose a 2-line script: "Were observing elevated load and have initiated temporary fallback routing. Well update every 15m and share telemetry/billing after stabilization."

vijay: I'll run a quick staging test to confirm the 3m trigger and post numbers.

ops-bot: CHECKLIST CREATED: reserved-pool-ga-checklist v1 -> https://internal.templates/reserved-pool-ga v1.0

maya: Next: SEs to use this on two pilots next week. Engineering to lock exact trigger thresholds by EOD Wed. If no objections Ill publish to the SE playbook.

drew: Fine by me. If we can, add a tiny state diagram to the slide too for visual clarity.
